subject: Iberian lynx
title: A Wild Lynx Gives Dead Rabbits a Bath. Scientists Think They Know Why

scenes.text: A wild cat in Spain does something no carnivore was ever seen doing.
It carries a dead rabbit to a water trough, and dunks it.
Camera traps caught it eight times, by five different female lynxes.
Most soaks lasted about a minute. The longest went past four minutes.
The rabbits weren't eaten there. They were carried away, and scientists think the mothers were feeding cubs.
A soaked rabbit is softer and full of water. Dinner and a drink in one, for cubs just leaving milk behind.

description:
Camera traps in central Spain caught wild Iberian lynxes dunking dead rabbits in water troughs, the first recorded case of a carnivore soaking its prey.
Between 2020 and 2025, five different females did it eight times, usually for about a minute and once for more than four. The leading ideas: the soaked rabbit carries water to cubs and is softer for kittens moving from milk to meat (Ecology, 2026).
Why do you think only these lynxes do it?
first_comment: Four of the eight soaks were by one female the scientists call Naia. Which animal habit should we look into next?
